title: fix(gateway): attribute ephemeral connections in normal logs
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Normal Gateway journals cannot attribute successful ephemeral connections: CLI/backend client metadata was verbose-only, while authenticated-user and webchat connection records overlapped.

## User Impact

Operators get one `client connected` record per admitted operator/node connection, including client ID/name, mode, role, authentication method, version/platform/build, remote address, and an authenticated user when present. Request content and credentials are excluded. Log consumers matching the old `authenticated user connected` or `webchat connected` messages should use the new record.

## Why This Change Was Made

This consolidates the existing three connection-log paths into one at the same admission boundary. No new registry, timer, cache, configuration, transport, authentication, or pairing path is introduced. Gateway-hosted node services and plugin requests already use in-process dispatch; their transport should not be rewritten without caller evidence. The docs explain persistent external polling and the existing plugin runtime APIs. The bundled node-connect skill now recognizes the unified admission record, including its distinction from hello delivery, and retains guidance for older deployed builds.

## Evidence

A read-only 30-minute diagnostic sample measured approximately 1,855 connects (61.85/min; 5.714 seconds of total handler time), 1,898 `chat.history` requests, and only 22 authenticated-user / 20 webchat connects (overlapping categories). Five-minute bursts closely tracked history requests; successful non-user client metadata was absent, so that correlation does not identify the caller. Four CPU profiles totaling about 20 seconds provided no sampled outgoing Gateway-client handshake and did contain existing in-process dispatch.

Before/after connection rate: unchanged by design; this fixes the missing attribution needed to select a transport change. No production deployment or same-services before/after load test was performed, and no connection-rate or latency improvement is claimed. A later deployed journal sample must identify the caller before reducing or batching its connects.

Production delta: 12 lines deleted net. The duplicate verbose/user/webchat emission paths are removed; backend admission visibility and authenticated-user attribution remain covered.

Validation: the backend regression failed before the change because there was no attributable normal-level connection record. After the change, all 49 tests in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.post-connect-health.test.ts` passed (75.25 s Vitest wall time, 82.48 s wrapper total; the new case took 530 ms). Changed-file oxfmt and core oxlint passed; `git diff --check` passed. An invalid unpaired CLI fixture was removed before final proof. The initial unscoped lint wrapper began unrelated plugin declaration preparation and was stopped; the explicit core-config run passed. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated; broad gates are delegated to PR CI.

Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, no accepted/actionable findings. Review and simplification preserved the admission boundary, existing redaction, and authenticated-user attribution. The focused skill correction also passed independent autoreview through P2. The production code and its 49-test proof are unchanged. Documentation scopes the record to operator/node connections: dedicated worker ingress does not use this admission path and its handshake does not contribute to the ordinary `connect` handler metric.


CI attribution: `check-guards` in run [38930368454](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38930368454/job/117073358503) fails because duplicate-scan target coverage omits `cli-parent-lifetime.mjs`. The automatic classifier labeled it new based on an older passing main job without comparing selected scope. The exact focused command `node scripts/check-duplicates.mjs --coverage` exits 1 with the same single uncovered filename on PR head `83a6f67b5310b09a426dd1e08ae291a581e66ece` and CI main parent `bb642e181e130153894a45f141a5368123bcd487`. The checker and omitted file are byte-identical between those revisions. Baseline execution used a task-owned temporary Git index populated with the exact parent via `git read-tree`; the checker reads only the tracked path inventory in coverage mode. No full duplicate scan or unrelated source repair was run. This is inherited baseline failure, not duplicated code added by this PR.


The first CI attempt also failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` at `src/flows/doctor-plugin-source-captures.test.ts:32`: its closed mock for `../process/supervisor/darwin-bun-process-census.js` is absent from the mock-export baseline. A focused diagnostic using the production native parser, import resolver, and `scanClosedMockFactories` on that single test produced the same fingerprint (`0f314816d50228e6240f1048998f802dd80d499ba91277a72f2a366e9c574dd2`), absent from the ledger, on both the PR and exact CI main parent. The failing test, scanner, and ledger are unchanged by this PR. The newer commit only fixes the bundled skill reference identified by review; it does not rerun CI merely to chase green.


Final validation: [CI run 38932919144](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38932919144) completed successfully on exact head `271226ce67ecc7c6482766bdd1ce226c82dd77b6`: all 34 executed jobs passed, including changed Node tests, UI E2E, docs, guards, lint, production/test types, security-fast, and the aggregate gate. Dependency and security-sensitive reviews also passed. The earlier inherited guard failures did not recur; no inherited-failure exception or CI rerun is needed. The final documentation scope correction passed independent autoreview through P2.
